rationale: The workflow already implements the evidence-supported P-LIT-GHA-CACHE optimization: it restores Gradle dependency caches (~/.gradle/caches keyed by dependency lockfiles) and the Gradle wrapper (~/.gradle/wrapper) before running ./gradlew build. The experiment evidence for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (Gradle case: batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200; Go case: batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9) measures the benefit of adding exactly this dependency-cache step, which is already present. The pattern's contraindication "An equivalent cache already exists" therefore applies, so re-adding it would be redundant and would not preserve a minimal change. Other candidate patterns do not fit: the matrix has a single JDK cell (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST offers no meaningful cancellation and every matrix outcome may be required), there is no evidence of runaway jobs warranting a custom timeout, and no change-path or test-selection evidence applies to this Gradle build. No new network access, secrets, publishing, or privileged actions are introduced.
